text: I'll start with the StatefulSet and the pending pod.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db asks for a StorageClass that does not exist in this cluster. Its volumeClaimTemplate "data" sets .spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", but the only StorageClass in the cluster is "standard" (the default, provisioner rancher.io/local-path). The generated PersistentVolumeClaim data-metrics-db-0 therefore stays Pending with ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found, and the scheduler refuses to place pod metrics-db-0 ("pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"), so the StatefulSet stays at 0/1 Ready and the headless Service metrics-db has no endpoint addresses, which is why dashboards are empty. Fix the storageClassName in the volumeClaimTemplate to "standard" (the volumeClaimTemplates field is immutable on a live StatefulSet, so the StatefulSet must be recreated — e.g. kubectl delete statefulset metrics-db --cascade=orphan — along with deleting the stuck PVC data-metrics-db-0 so it is regenerated against the correct class).
arguments.mechanism: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db sets .spec.volumeClaimTemplates[0].spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", a StorageClass that does not exist in this cluster (only "standard" does), so the PersistentVolumeClaim it generates, data-metrics-db-0, is rejected by the persistentvolume-controller with ProvisioningFailed "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found" and stays Pending unbound; its pod metrics-db-0 is left unschedulable on unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims and the StatefulSet reports 0/1 Ready.

evidence.claim: StatefulSet metrics-db is 0/1 Ready and its pod is unscheduled and Pending.
The pod cannot be scheduled because its PVC is unbound.
evidence.quote: 0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims.

evidence.claim: The StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplate requests StorageClass fast-ssd.
The generated PVC is Pending because the named StorageClass does not exist.
evidence.quote: Warning  ProvisioningFailed  1s (x2 over 1s)  persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

evidence.claim: The only StorageClass in the cluster is standard, which is the default.

ruled_out.alternative: The Service selector does not match the pod labels, so endpoints are empty for a labeling reason.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service selector {app=metrics-db} matches the pod's labels exactly; the endpoints are empty only because no pod is running.

ruled_out.alternative: The node is out of capacity or tainted, so the pod cannot be scheduled.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node is Ready with full allocatable CPU, memory and 110 pod slots and no taints listed; scheduling failed on volume binding, not capacity.
ruled_out.quote:
node/incident-lab-control-plane cpu=6/6 memory=12220316Ki/12220316Ki pods=110 (capacity/allocatable)
  condition Ready=True

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken, causing crash/pull failure.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never reached a node at all — PodScheduled is False and no container ever started, so image and command play no part.

verification.command: kubectl -n analytics get statefulset metrics-db -o json

arguments.root_cause_statement: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db asks for a StorageClass that does not exist in this cluster. Its volumeClaimTemplate "data" sets .spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", but the only StorageClass in the cluster is "standard" (the default, provisioner rancher.io/local-path). The PersistentVolumeClaim data-metrics-db-0 generated from that template therefore stays Pending with ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found, and the scheduler refuses to place the StatefulSet's pod ("pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"), so the workload stays at 0/1 Ready and the headless Service metrics-db has no endpoint addresses, which is why dashboards are empty. Fix the storageClassName in the volumeClaimTemplate to "standard"; because volumeClaimTemplates are immutable on a live StatefulSet, apply it by recreating the StatefulSet (kubectl delete statefulset metrics-db --cascade=orphan) and deleting the stuck PersistentVolumeClaim data-metrics-db-0 so it is regenerated against the correct class.
arguments.mechanism: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db sets .spec.volumeClaimTemplates[0].spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", a StorageClass that does not exist in this cluster, so the PersistentVolumeClaim it generates, data-metrics-db-0, is rejected by the persistentvolume-controller with ProvisioningFailed "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found" and stays Pending and unbound. With that volume never binding, the StatefulSet's replica cannot be scheduled onto any node and the StatefulSet reports 0/1 Ready.
